subject: Hosted latency baseline & p95/p99 handoff — post-demo clarifications
messages:
From: Michael Torres <michael.torres@atlashealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-01T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: latency targets and streaming behavior

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo this morning. The product team liked the flow, but they left with two sticky items we need clarified before we bring procurement in:

- Our primary concern is end-to-end latency for short requests (user message -> model token response). We need to understand p95 and p99 with our traffic mix (attached a sample envelope).
- We also need guidance on concurrency limits and streaming behavior. We have many concurrent users typing while others are long-polling for streaming updates.

Attached: atlas_traffic_profile_q1.csv (sample of real traffic we can share). Can you send a concise test plan and what you’d need from us to validate p95/p99 against the hosted API vs our current provider?

Looking to align timing — ideally get a short POC next week. Looping Alice from engineering who owns the traffic shaping.

Thanks,
Michael
Michael Torres
Director of Platform Engineering
Atlas Health
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Michael Torres <michael.torres@atlashealth.com>, Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-02T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: latency targets and streaming behavior

Hi Michael / Alice — thanks for the traffic sample and the clear asks. Quick read-through and a proposed approach below. I kept this deliberately short so we can move to a POC schedule quickly.

Summary of what we’ll validate for hosted vs incumbent:
- p95 and p99 end-to-end (client -> Redwood hosted API -> model -> client) for three request classes: short (1-3 tokens output), medium (10-40 tokens), long (100+ tokens).
- Concurrency envelope: 50 / 200 / 500 concurrent active sessions (you said peak ~350).
- Streaming: measure tail impact when N streams are active and when a subset uses long-lived streams plus intermittent bursts.

What we need from Atlas:
- Confirm the CSV is representative (it looks great). If you have per-route latency SLOs, attach those.
- Provide a 48-hour window where we can replay the envelope (or send live traffic to a test route).
- If procurement needs a cost estimate for a POC, tell us target duration and concurrency cap.

Proposed Redwood deliverables for the POC (1-week technical spike):
- Controlled traffic replay of your envelope against a hosted test instance.
- p95/p99 matrix by request class and concurrency bucket, incl. streaming breakdown.
- Simple fallback/rollout recommendation if any route exceeds thresholds (model variant, batching changes, or routing to a different capacity tier).
- Recording of the test run + CSV of raw latencies.

I attached a lightweight test plan (baseline_test_matrix.xlsx) and a recording of the demo for reference (redwood_demo-recording.mp4).

Next steps: if this sounds good, I’ll loop in Jonas (performance eng) and Karthik (solutions) to scope the traffic replay and concrete time windows. Can you confirm a preferred test week?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-03T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo: latency targets and streaming behavior — quick sizing ask

Karthik / Jonas — forwarding Atlas’ traffic sample and a short ask from Michael: they want p95/p99 baseline numbers and a POC next week if possible. Key constraints:
- Peak concurrent sessions ~350, typical blend skewed to short/medium outputs.
- Streaming clients: ~30% of sessions maintain an open stream for typing; bursty writes otherwise.

Can you help with a quick sizing and the specific test harness we should run against hosted? Also note: procurement may ask for an estimate of cost/credits for a 5-7 day POC.

Questions for your reply (just bullet answers suffice):
1) What test matrix (concurrency buckets + request classes) should we run to produce defensible p95/p99 numbers?
2) For hosted API, any config knobs we should toggle (batching window, kv-cache size, streaming concurrency cap)?
3) Any red flags given the traffic sample?

If easier, we can triage on a quick 20-min sync — I’ll coordinate after your reply.

Thanks — Marissa
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-04T16:50:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-demo: latency targets and streaming behavior — quick sizing ask

Marissa / Jonas — quick answers and a proposed minimal matrix. Kept it pragmatic so we can scope the POC cost.

1) Test matrix (minimal, defensible):
   - Request classes: short (1-3 out tokens), medium (10-40), long (100+).
   - Concurrency buckets: 50, 250, 500 (covers their stated peak ~350).
   - Streaming scenarios: a) 0% streaming (baseline), b) 30% streaming steady-state, c) 30% streaming + 20% burst (10s bursts every 2 min).

2) Hosted config knobs to seed:
   - Batching: start with 10ms continuous batching, then 25ms for a secondary run to show tradeoffs.
   - KV-cache: enable prefix caching for repeated prompts; for their workload we’ll set a 512-entry cache per host.
   - Streaming concurrency cap: enforce 500 total open streams per zone, with backpressure at 600 to measure behavior.

3) Red flags from traffic:
   - Envelope has many short requests interleaved with long tails — looks like a chat + summarization mix. The main risk is tail amplification when many long requests pile behind small batching windows.
   - Recommendation: include a run with slightly increased batching (25ms) to show cost/latency tradeoff and a run with KV-cache disabled to show worst-case.

POC sizing and rough credit estimate (hosted):
   - 5-day run using the matrix above, controlled replay: we estimate ~12k GPU-minutes across the test window (variable by model choice).
   - Ballpark hosted credit ask for procurement: $6k–$9k for the technical spike (includes increased priority for capacity during replay).

If that works I’ll wire up the replay harness and share the test plan spreadsheet with concrete time slots.

— Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-demo: latency targets and streaming behavior — POC proposal and next steps

Hi Michael / Alice — glad to sync the internal recommendations above. TL;DR: we can run a focused, 5-day technical spike next week that will produce p95/p99 matrices for hosted vs incumbent, plus streaming delta numbers. Below is the concrete plan and asks so procurement can scope budget.

What Redwood will deliver (5-day POC):
- Replay-run of your atlas_traffic_profile_q1.csv across the matrix Karthik outlined (50 / 250 / 500 concurrency, three request classes, three streaming scenarios).
- Per-route p95/p99 CSV + annotated notes where we see notable tail amplification.
- Demo + recording of the run (we’ll share redwood_demo-recording.mp4 link) and one 30-minute wrap to go through results.
- Short prescriptive appendix: recommended batch window, caching profile, and rollout guardrails for production.

What we need from Atlas to start:
1) Final confirmation that the attached CSV is the correct envelope to replay (or an updated file).
2) A 4-hour window where Atlas can accept increased load to a test route OR permission to run the replay from our side against a supplied test endpoint.
3) Procurement confirmation on budget for a $7k hosted credit (we estimated $6k–$9k) to cover priority capacity for the spike. If procurement prefers a narrower scope, we can cut to a 3-day run focusing on 50/250 buckets only.

Logistics & links:
